arc: Man in a hole: a run upstream with an old fish as the pond starts to drain (-1), a false spring (+2) that turns out to be a greenhouse drain (-1), the old fish stops in the reeds (-3, the bottom at 0.71), the home pond is drained away (-2), the cold spring (+2).
note: Scenes open in src/journey.c at fixed progress points (a reach starts, a reach is cleared, the halfway mark of the last reach); the words are in web/app.js. The physics in fluid.c and swimmer.c is unchanged; story beats change only the sluice jet strength and the stamina budget. The actual order per seed is in play-order.json, story numbers on/off and per choice path in ablation.json, per-reach crises and sweeps in tension.json, all written by make story. tests/test_story.c checks the order, every [mech] number and the [quiet] heavy scenes; make test re-runs bench rows and requires them verbatim. Emotion values were re-scored by an independent reviewer (claude-reviewer, 2026-11-02) from the scene text in web/app.js and the effects in src/journey.c.

characters.want: to keep up with Silt and reach the spring before the pond is gone
characters.need: to stop beating its tail without rest: push, then let go, and set the pace for someone else
characters.start: races ahead and cheers at the first warm water
characters.end: waits at the mouth of the spring, pushing when the water pushes, for the next small fish (or alone, listening for a tail that does not come)

characters.want: one more run to the spring
characters.need: to hand the way on before his fins give out
characters.end: stays behind in the reeds and lets Copperfin go on

beats.summary: The outlet board is lifted and the pond starts to drain. Silt sets the pace: strokes cost less while he swims with you.
beats.evidence: Push when I push. Rest when I rest.

beats.summary: The stream splits: a short pipe that squeezes the jet (hard water, quick), or the slack ditch round the field (easy water, cheap strokes) with a weir halfway where Copperfin must hold inside a ring for 18 s of swimming while the current keeps running.

labels: Squeeze through the pipe (hard water, quick)
Go round by the ditch (easy water, hold at the weir)

beats.evidence: It squeezes the water, and the water squeezes you.

beats.summary: A back-eddy behind a stone. They rest; the stamina reserve fills past full (1.5) and lasts through the warm water.
Warm still water. Copperfin thinks they have made it.
Silt tastes it: the spring is never warm. It is the greenhouse drain, and warm water gives the breath back slowly (recovery x0.12).
beats.evidence: The spring is never warm. This is the glasshouse drain.

beats.summary: Silt's fins are done. He stays in the reeds. Stay with him until he breathes easier (a 22 s hold in the reeds while the current runs; stamina back and faster recovery, but the last board comes out as you leave), or leave before the second board comes out (it comes out at the halfway mark, weaker).

labels: Stay beside Silt until he breathes easier (the last board comes out while you wait)
Leave now, before the second board comes out

beats.summary: The last board comes out (at the halfway mark, or as Copperfin leaves the reeds after staying): the jet grows and the home pond is gone for good.
beats.evidence: That was home. You could have waited one more day.

beats.summary: Cold water all at once. Copperfin pushes, then lets go; the ending depends on what it did in the reeds.
beats.evidence: The water turns cold all at once. Colder than your fins.

text: Copperfin pushes once, then lets go, and the spring carries it the last length.
Silt's gills were moving slow and even.
Now it waits at the mouth of the spring, pushing when the water pushes, resting when it rests, for whatever small thing comes up the pipe next.
Copperfin pushes, then lets go, and the spring takes the last length.
It never looked back to see whether Silt
The light held. That was the trade.
It keeps to the mouth of the spring alone, listening for a second tail in the dark water. None comes.
